subtitle: When Thanesar’s Prince Faced Gauda’s Lion over the Thrones of the Ganga

panels.shot: wide, dramatic split-composition showing two distant cities on either side of a broad river plain, one with banners of Thanesar-Kannauj, the other with Gauda emblems, Harsha in the foreground holding a spear and looking toward a blazing funerary pyre far away
panels.action: Harsha Vardhana stands in the foreground in war attire, half-lit by the glow of a distant pyre on the horizon, as two rival cityscapes of Kannauj and Gauda loom on opposite sides of the riverine plains beneath a stormy sky.

dialogue.text: Out of a brother’s death and a sister’s peril, Harsha and Shashanka turned the middle Ganga into a chessboard; this is how grief and rivalry remade Kannauj.

i18n.hi: भाई की मौत और बहन के संकट से हर्ष और शशांक ने मध्य गंगा को शतरंज बना दिया; ऐसे ही शोक और दुश्मनी ने कन्नौज को बदल डाला।

panels.shot: epic bird’s-eye over North India, with faded outlines of older Gupta domains dissolving into smaller crowns around the Ganga-Yamuna doab and Bengal
panels.action: A map-like vista of North India shows the once-unified Gupta realm breaking into many crowns, banners of Thanesar, Kannauj and Gauda rising amid rivers and forests under a hazy dawn.

dialogue.text: After the Guptas, the north was no single lion’s den. Thanesar, Kannauj and Gauda watched each other across the Ganga, each hungry for the vacant imperial seat.

i18n.hi: गुप्तों के बाद उत्तर कोई एक शेर की मांद नहीं रहा। थानेसर, कन्नौज और गौड़ गंगा पार एक-दूसरे पर नज़र गड़ाए थे, सब उस खाली सम्राट-आसन के भूखे।

panels.shot: medium shot in a royal hall at Thanesar, young Harsha in simple princely robes beside an elder king figure (not named), with maps and war standards in the background
panels.action: Young Harsha Vardhana stands alert beside his seated father in the palace of Thanesar, scrolls and spears lining the hall as ministers gesture toward the routes leading to Kannauj.

dialogue.text: In Thanesar, the Vardhanas rose, first as protectors of the region, then as kings. Harsha was the younger prince, watching borders and listening to tales of Kannauj.

i18n.hi: थानेसर में वर्धन उठे, पहले रक्षक बनकर, फिर राजे बन गए। हर्ष छोटा राजकुमार था, सरहदें देखता, कन्नौज की कहानियाँ सुनता।

panels.shot: wide shot of a bustling cityscape of Kannauj on the Ganga, its ghats busy, its palace prominent, banners with a distinct emblem fluttering
panels.action: The city of Kannauj spreads along the riverbank, merchants and boats crowding the ghats while atop a fortified hill a royal palace watches the waterway like a jewel in the plains.

dialogue.text: Kannauj, ruled by the Maukharis, sat like a gem on the Ganga. Whoever held it could call himself arbiter of the middle plains.

i18n.hi: मौखरियों का कन्नौज गंगा किनारे जड़े रत्न जैसा था। जिसे ये मिले, वही मध्य मैदानों का न्यायकर्ता समझा जाता।

panels.shot: transition montage: Thanesar and Kannauj linked by a marriage procession, with a palanquin and bride moving between banners of both houses
panels.action: A royal marriage procession winds along a dusty road, palanquin in the center, banners of Thanesar and Kannauj raised together as drums and conch shells herald the alliance.

dialogue.text: To bind this jewel, Thanesar and Kannauj joined dynasties by marriage. For a moment, crowns that once rivalled each other spoke of kinship and shared defense.

i18n.hi: इस रत्न को बाँधने को थानेसर और कन्नौज ने शादियों से वंश जोड़े। कुछ पल को जो ताज दुश्मन थे, वे रिश्तेदारी और साझा रक्षा की बात करने लगे।

panels.shot: medium shot of a messenger covered in dust arriving breathless at a court; behind him, a faint vision of a fallen king on a battlefield
panels.action: A dust-streaked messenger bursts into a lamplit hall, hands still shaking, while behind him in ghostly overlay we glimpse a king lying still on a trampled field.

dialogue.text: Then news came like a storm breaking: the Maukhari king had fallen. Between friend and rival, the line blurred, and Kannauj’s throne trembled once more.

i18n.hi: फिर खबर बिजली-सी गिरी: मौखरी नरेश मारे गए। दोस्त और प्रतिद्वंदी में रेखा धुंधली हुई, और कन्नौज का सिंहासन फिर डगमगाया।

panels.shot: close-up on Harsha’s face, shadowed, as he hears of his elder brother’s death, with a faint reflection of a funeral pyre in his eyes
panels.action: Harsha Vardhana is shown in close profile, jaw set and eyes dark, the distant glow of a pyre reflected in his gaze as an unseen voice speaks of Rajyavardhana’s death.

dialogue.text: Soon after, Harsha’s world cracked again. His elder brother Rajyavardhana, who had ridden out in that chaos, did not return.

i18n.hi: ज़्यादा देर नहीं, हर्ष की दुनिया फिर टूटी। उसका बड़ा भाई राज्यवर्धन, जो उस हलचल में निकला था, लौटकर नहीं आया।

panels.shot: wide shot of a riverbank at dusk with a tall funeral pyre blazing; Harsha stands rigid, in white mourning cloth over his armour, hands clenched
panels.action: On the banks of a wide river at dusk, a great pyre burns, its flames rising into smoky sky, while Harsha stands before it between armour and mourning cloth, fists tight at his sides.

dialogue.text: Bana, Harsha’s poet, speaks of a prince who stood by the pyre and felt grief harden into iron. He says Harsha named a culprit and swore revenge.

i18n.hi: बाण, हर्ष का कवि, उस राजकुमार का ज़िक्र करता है जो चिता के पास खड़ा रहा और जिसका शोक लोहा बन गया। कहता है, हर्ष ने दुश्मन ठहराया और बदले की सौगंध ली।

panels.shot: medium close-up, Harsha’s face lit by flames, hand raised as if in oath, background blurred
panels.action: Harsha raises his right hand slightly toward the flames, eyes steady and shining with tears, as sparks rise and the dark silhouettes of retainers watch in silence.

dialogue.speaker: Harsha Vardhana
dialogue.text: Brother, I will not rest while those who moved against us sit unchallenged.

i18n.hi: भैया, जब तक हम पर वार करने वाले बेख़ौफ़ बैठे हैं, मैं चैन से नहीं बैठूँगा।

panels.shot: juxtaposed panels-within-panel style: on one side, a stern Harsha with Bana by his side; on the other, a neutral scholar reading inscriptions and coins laid out
panels.action: On one side Bana bows slightly near a resolute Harsha in a court hall; on the other, a calm later scholar leans over copper plates and Gauda coins glinting on a table.

dialogue.text: Harsha’s court blamed Shashanka of Gauda for treachery. But the inscriptions and coins tell us something plainer: Gauda was strong, and its king was no shadow villain.

i18n.hi: हर्ष के दरबार ने गौड़ के शशांक को दगाबाज़ ठहराया। पर अभिलेखों और सिक्कों में बस इतना साफ है: गौड़ ताकतवर था, उसका राजा कोई पर्दे का खलनायक नहीं।

panels.shot: epic bird’s-eye of Gauda’s capital in Bengal, with lush greenery, a fortified city and the sea of the Ganga delta beyond
panels.action: A fortified city rises amid the lush green of Bengal’s plains, moats and ramparts guarding tall halls, as the braided channels of the Ganga stretch toward a misted horizon.

dialogue.text: In the east, Shashanka ruled Gauda from a rich delta. His seals and coins show a kingdom that minted its own power and vied for influence in the same contested plains.

i18n.hi: पूरब में शशांक समृद्ध डेल्टा से गौड़ चलाता था। उसकी मुहरें और सिक्के दिखाते हैं कि ये राज्य खुद अपनी ताकत गढ़ता था और इन्हीं झगड़ालू मैदानों पर दबदबे की होड़ में था।

panels.shot: medium shot of Shashanka seated on a throne in a Bengal-style hall, advisors around him, a map of the middle Ganga on a cloth before them
panels.action: Shashanka sits upright on a carved throne in a hall open to the wind, advisors gathered as they study a cloth map marked with rivers and the name of Kannauj between Gauda and Thanesar.

dialogue.text: Between Banabhatta’s accusations and later retellings, Shashanka became a convenient villain. Yet the contest he and Harsha waged was for crowns and corridors, not for faith alone.

i18n.hi: बाणभट्ट के आरोपों से लेकर बाद की कहानियों तक, शशांक आसान खलनायक बना दिया गया। पर जिस जंग वो और हर्ष लड़ रहे थे, वो ताजों और राहों की थी, सिर्फ मज़हब की नहीं।

panels.shot: wide shot of Harsha being anointed or crowned in Thanesar, priests and ministers surrounding, the mood both solemn and tense
panels.action: In the main hall of Thanesar, Harsha bows as sacred water is poured over his head, ministers watching with grave faces while warriors clutch spears at the edges of the ceremony.

dialogue.text: At about sixteen, Harsha was raised as king. In one stroke he inherited Thanesar’s crown, Maukhari alliance through his sister, and a tangle of rival claims around Kannauj.

i18n.hi: लगभग सोलह पर ही हर्ष को राजगद्दी मिली। एक झटके में उसने थानेसर का ताज, बहन के ज़रिए मौखरी संग का नाता, और कन्नौज के चारों तरफ़ उलझी दावेदारी संभाल ली।

panels.shot: dynamic low-angle of Harsha mounting a war elephant, armour being strapped on, troops forming lines behind him on an open plain
panels.action: Harsha climbs onto a war elephant as attendants tighten straps and place a parasol above him, while lines of cavalry and foot soldiers form in the background on a sunbaked plain.

dialogue.text: He did not sit still. Harsha gathered Thanesar’s men, rallied the Maukhari remnants, and turned west, north and east in quick campaigns that would stitch a new realm.

i18n.hi: वो चुप न बैठा। हर्ष ने थानेसर के सिपाही जुटाए, बचे-कुचे मौखरी दल को साधा, और पश्चिम, उत्तर, पूरब तीनों ओर तेज़ मुहिम चला कर नया राज्य बुनने लगा।

panels.shot: sweeping wide shot of two armies facing off across a river crossing or ford, banners of Gauda and Harsha’s house visible, but no actual clash shown
panels.action: Across a shallow river ford two armies glare at one another, elephants and cavalry massed on both banks, with distinct banners of Gauda on one side and of Harsha’s line on the other.

dialogue.text: Bana speaks of sudden attacks, cunning retreats, and Gauda’s forces checked. But he gives no single, clear day of decision; the struggle was a campaign, not one neat battle.

i18n.hi: बाण अचानक धावे, चालाक पीछे हटना, और गौड़ की टुकड़ियों को रोके जाने की बातें करता है। पर वो कोई एक साफ़ निर्णायक दिन नहीं बताता; ये जंग एक पूरा अभियान था, कोई एक साफ लड़ाई नहीं।

panels.shot: montage-like shot: Harsha’s forces marching through forests, crossing rivers, entering cities; each small vignette hints at different fronts
panels.action: Multiple vignettes fill the frame—a column crossing a forest road, another fording a river, a third entering a walled town—conveying Harsha’s armies moving across varied lands.

dialogue.text: What our sources agree on is the effect: over years, Harsha secured the middle Ganga, checked rivals like Shashanka, and drew smaller crowns into his orbit.

i18n.hi: हमारे स्रोत असर पर सहमत हैं: बरसों में हर्ष ने मध्य गंगा संभाली, शशांक जैसे प्रतिद्वंद्वियों को रोका, और छोटे ताजों को अपने घेरे में खींच लिया।

panels.shot: wide interior shot of Kannauj’s royal hall, now clearly under new rule, with envoys from different regions presenting gifts
panels.action: Within Kannauj’s audience hall, envoys from distant regions kneel with tribute—ivory, textiles, and scrolls—while the throne at the far end is occupied by a figure in Harsha’s style of regalia.

dialogue.text: From Thanesar’s smaller court, Harsha shifted his weight to Kannauj. Xuanzang would later describe this city as the beating heart of his empire, where roads from many lands met.

i18n.hi: थानेसर के छोटे दरबार से हर्ष ने अपना भार कन्नौज पर डाला। बाद में ह्वेनसांग ने इसे उसके साम्राज्य का धड़कता दिल लिखा, जहाँ कई दिशाओं से आती सड़कें मिलती थीं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Xuanzang standing on a terrace in Kannauj, looking out over the city, with monks and officials around him
panels.action: Xuanzang stands on a high terrace beside local guides, his robes stirred by the wind, as he looks over the spread of Kannauj’s temples, markets and palaces under a clear sky.

dialogue.text: The Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang saw a vast realm under Harsha, stretching from the Himalaya foothills down the Ganga, and he named Shashanka as a rival still holding Gauda in the east.

i18n.hi: चीनी यात्री ह्वेनसांग ने हर्ष के अधीन फैला विशाल इलाका देखा, जो हिमालय की तराइयों से गंगा के निचले हिस्सों तक जाता था, और उसने पूर्व में गौड़ पकड़े बैठे शशांक को अब भी प्रतिद्वंदी लिखा।

panels.shot: split composition showing Harsha’s administrative copper plates being inscribed on one side and Shashanka’s coin being struck on the other
panels.action: On one side scribes etch lettering into a gleaming copper plate under Harsha’s seal; on the other, a die strikes a coin bearing Shashanka’s emblem in a modest mint workshop.

dialogue.text: Harsha’s copper plates and Shashanka’s coins survive side by side, two rulers writing themselves into metal. Each line reminds us that history’s victors did not erase every rival.

i18n.hi: हर्ष की ताम्रपट्टियाँ और शशांक के सिक्के आज भी साथ-साथ मिलते हैं, दो राजा जो खुद को धातु में दर्ज कर रहे थे। हर पंक्ति याद दिलाती है कि इतिहास के विजेताओं ने हर विरोधी को मिटा नहीं दिया।

panels.shot: close-up on Harsha older, seated in thought, scrolls and a globe-like map near him, expression calmer yet marked by memory
panels.action: An older Harsha sits on a cushioned seat, a large map and scrolls spread nearby, his hand resting on his knee as he gazes ahead with a mix of weariness and steady resolve.

dialogue.text: From the oath by the pyre to the canopy over Kannauj, Harsha’s arc runs through grief and ambition. Yet his story also warns us to look past court tales when we weigh blame.

i18n.hi: चिता के सामने उठे प्रण से लेकर कन्नौज की छत्रछाया तक, हर्ष की राह शोक और महत्वाकांक्षा के बीच से गुजरती है। पर उसकी कहानी ये भी सिखाती है कि इलज़ाम तौलते वक्त सिर्फ दरबारी किस्सों पर न टिकें।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot of the Ganga plain at sunset, Kannauj and the distant east suggested as silhouettes, the river calm and broad
panels.action: The Ganga glides wide and calm under a red-gold sunset, faint silhouettes of a city like Kannauj on one bank and distant eastern hills on the other, while birds cross the glowing sky.

dialogue.text: Harsha and Shashanka show us that power born from loss can reshape a land, but only when read through evidence and restraint do their rival oaths become wisdom for our own age.

i18n.hi: हर्ष और शशांक दिखाते हैं कि खोने से जन्मी ताकत भी ज़मीन बदल सकती है, पर सबूत और संयम से पढ़ें तो ही उनके टकराते प्रण हमारी अपनी उम्र के लिए सीख बनते हैं।

title_i18n.hi: चिता के सामने लिया गया प्रण

subtitle_i18n.en: When Thanesar’s Prince Faced Gauda’s Lion over the Thrones of the Ganga
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब थानेसर का राजकुमार गंगाकी गद्दियों पर गौड़ के शेर से भिड़ा
